title: Unsafe file upload with bounded proof
summary: Use a benign canary file and prove public retrieval or browser execution before reporting impact.
steps: Select an observed upload form or API in scope; use a disposable test account and record the normal filename, MIME, and size rules.
Upload a small benign text canary first, then one controlled mismatch of extension, declared content type, or file signature at a time.
For HTML execution, use only a tiny file that calls alert with the fresh aegis-verify canary; never upload a shell or destructive payload.

Retrieve the resulting URL in a clean browser session and verify actual script execution with browser_xss evidence. Use upload_xss proof with upload_id, read_id, browser_id, and cleanup_id. A 200 upload response, filename echo, or raw HTML reflection is only a lead.
For unauthorized file access, replay the same uploaded object under a distinct verified identity and apply authorization proof.
Delete the test object and verify cleanup. If cleanup is unavailable, stop and report the residual test artifact to the analyst.
Submit a candidate only with upload, retrieval, execution or authorization, and cleanup evidence IDs.
pass_signals: Uploaded active content executes in the browser at a same-origin retrieval URL
A foreign identity retrieves a known private uploaded object
kill_signals: Upload rejected or normalized to inert content
Retrieval forces a download or sandboxed origin
Only filename or Content-Type reflection observed
